convertibility_reason: Martingale/grid position sizing with margin-dependent lot scaling, interactive tester panel with chart button controls, tick-level UI polling for button state, and broker-specific stop level checks make this inherently MT5-dependent

long.left: User clicks Buy button on tester panel

short.left: User clicks Sell button on tester panel

other_exits: When 2+ buy positions exist, all buy TPs are modified to factb + CORR (weighted average price plus TPPlus offset including stopLevel)
When 2+ sell positions exist, all sell TPs are modified to facts - CORR (weighted average price minus TPPlus offset including stopLevel)
Trailing stop only operates when exactly 1 position of that side exists

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Initial trade uses input Lots. Martingale layers multiply the smallest (buy) or largest (sell) existing position lot by nextLot^count, creating exponential lot increase on each averaging layer.

custom_logic_notes: This is a manual/semi-automated Strategy Tester EA. Entry is triggered by clicking Buy/Sell buttons on a chart panel. The 'Martingale' button toggles automatic averaging: when price moves StepPips against the best (lowest buy / highest sell) position, a new martingale-scaled position is opened with SL=0 and TP=0. All positions of the same direction then have their TP modified to the volume-weighted average entry price +/- (TPPlus + stopLevel) * point. The 'Trail' button toggles trailing stop logic that only applies when exactly one position of that direction exists. The trailing logic has two phases: initial trail activation (price must exceed open by TrailingStop + TrailingStep - 1*point) and subsequent step moves (price must exceed current SL by TrailingStep + 5*point). Swap and commission are factored into the weighted average price calculation. The EA exclusively runs in Strategy Tester visual mode and refuses to run on live/demo charts. Magic number is hardcoded to 0.
python_conversion_notes: The core martingale averaging logic (weighted average price, exponential lot scaling, TP modification to breakeven+TPPlus) is convertible. However, the interactive button-based entry system has no Python equivalent - entries would need to be replaced with automated signal logic or a different trigger mechanism. The trailing stop's two-phase logic and the swap-inclusive average price calculation are complex. The tester-only restriction (MQLInfoInteger(MQL_TESTER)) and OnTick button polling pattern would need removal. Margin check and lot validation functions are straightforward to replicate. The stopLevel inclusion in CORR calculation is broker-dependent and needs careful handling in Python backtests.
